extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners / patent prosecution trainees
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for conducting examination of U.S. patent applications, including examiner duties, statutory and regulatory bases for rejections, office action content, applicant responses, appeal/RCE practice, and allowance/issue procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of the patent examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: To serve as advocate/protector of the public interest with respect to intellectual property; to provide direct service and assistance to customers from inside and outside the USPTO; to serve as a judge on patentability with respect to invention(s) claimed in a patent application under the conditions for patentability set forth in Title 35 of the United States Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner responsibilities include balancing public interest and applicant rights, applying statutory conditions for patentability, and interacting with stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand application status terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and distinctions for Allowed, Patented, Abandoned, Published patent application, and Pendency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed = application indicated by an examiner as meeting statutory and regulatory requirements (not yet issued). Patented = issued on issue date. Abandoned = no longer pending and not patented (may be express or for failure to respond). Published application = PGPub under 35 U.S.C. §122(b). Pendency = time from filing date until issue or abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-search and search responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Searches existing technology for claimed invention; reads and understands the invention set forth in the specification; determines whether the application is adequate to define the metes and bounds of the claimed invention; determines the scope of the claim(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On taking up an application the examiner must make a thorough study and investigation of available prior art (37 CFR 1.104). Proper characterization of the invention and claim scope is foundational to examination and any subsequent rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing office actions and establishing the office's position
rubrics_metrics.description: Writes office actions identifying and analyzing all issues pertinent to patentability of the claimed invention; responds completely to applicant’s reply; issues notice of allowance or notice of abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office actions must identify and analyze grounds for objections/rejections and be responsive to applicant replies; the examiner is responsible for moving the prosecution to allowance or abandonment as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office action as a legal record
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets forth the legal basis for any objections, rejections, and indications of allowable subject matter; available to the public (if published); relied upon in court proceedings; aids public and courts with prosecution history rationale; must be consistent with office policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office actions should cite legal bases and be consistent with MPEP, published Guidelines, and applicable internal positions. Their content has evidentiary and precedential consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply statutes (35 U.S.C.) correctly
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutes (Title 35 U.S.C.) are enacted law and provide the basis for rejections; the USPTO cannot waive or interpret laws inconsistent with binding case law. If twice rejected, applicant may appeal to PTAB and then seek judicial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner rejections must be grounded in 35 U.S.C. provisions where applicable, and examiners must be mindful of appeal routes (PTAB, CAFC, ED Va.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply rules (37 CFR) for objections and petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules (Title 37 CFR) govern examination procedures; the USPTO may interpret or waive rules in certain instances; CFR is the basis for objections to any part of an application; once a requirement is made final, applicants may petition the examiner’s holding under MPEP Chapter 1000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner actions invoking procedural objections should reference relevant 37 CFR provisions and follow petition procedures where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for rejection — 35 U.S.C. §101 (statutory subject matter and related requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions patentable: must fall within one of four categories (process, machine, article of manufacture, composition of matter or improvements), not be directed to a judicial exception without additional limitations amounting to significantly more; proper inventorship named; specific, substantial, and credible utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should evaluate eligibility under §101 considering judicial exceptions and the 'significantly more' test, as well as inventorship and utility requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for rejection — 35 U.S.C. §112 (specification and claim requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specification requirements: written description, enablement, best mode. Claim requirements: content must 'particularly point out' (not vague) and 'distinctly claim' (not indefinite). Claim format: independent, dependent, multiple dependent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must assess written description and enablement support for claimed subject matter, identify lack of best mode if applicable, and evaluate claim definiteness and proper claim format per §112.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for rejection — 35 U.S.C. §102 (novelty / anticipation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty (new); Anticipation (no difference); defines what is 'prior' art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether a single prior art reference anticipates a claim; determine what qualifies as prior art for the application under §102.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for rejection — 35 U.S.C. §103 (non-obviousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-obvious is a legal determination that involves the concept of 'one of ordinary skill in the pertinent art'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must articulate reasoning why claimed subject matter would have been obvious to a POSITA, using proper factual underpinnings and legal standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art sources and applicant-admitted prior art (AAPA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Common prior art: patents (foreign/domestic), patent application publications (international/foreign/domestic), non-patent literature (books, journals, web-based publications); another type is applicant admitted prior art (AAPA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should search and rely on appropriate categories of prior art and consider admissions in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanisms by which art is made part of the application record
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR provisions that bring art into the record: 1.104 (nature of examination), 1.56 (duty to disclose information material to patentability), 1.97 (Filing of information disclosure statement), 1.98 (Content of IDS), 1.290 (third-party preissuance submissions), 1.105 (requirements for information).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand examiner obligations under 1.104 and the applicant/third-party duties/procedures for submitting prior art (IDS, third-party submissions), including timing limits (e.g., 1.290: within six months after PGPub date or up to first rejection in certain circumstances).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office action components and identification of type
rubrics_metrics.description: Office action summary sheet includes listing of attachments; detailed reasons and support for why applicant is not entitled to a patent accompany the summary sheet; note type of office action (non-final or final) and the shortened statutory period (SSP) for reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office actions must clearly identify attachments, substantive reasons for rejections/objections, whether action is final or non-final, and the statutory period for response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant's response requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant must answer all formal objections and rejections; contain amendments and/or arguments (generally both); amendments must be filed timely in accordance with the SSP and 37 CFR §1.136; 37 CFR §1.121 governs manner of making amendments; response must be signed by the authorized individual (attorney or pro se applicant).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should ensure responses comply with timing, signature, amendment format (sample amendment format available), and address all issues raised in the office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final office action characteristics and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: A final office action may occur on second (or later) examination if there are claims that are not allowable; notifies applicant of examiner’s final patentability determination; could include objections, rejections, and/or indication of allowable subject matter; sets SSP for response; prosecution is considered closed; further amendment after final is restricted (37 CFR §1.113 & §1.116).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final actions close prosecution and limit amendments; examiners should state grounds clearly and note available post-final options for applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid abandonment applicant options include: filing a reply after final action (§1.116), appealing any rejections (§41.31), or filing a request for continued examination (RCE) (§1.114).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should be aware of and advise on procedural paths available to applicants after final rejection and the related MPEP references (e.g., MPEP 714.13(II)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal practice (PTAB)
rubrics_metrics.description: A notice of appeal may be filed after any of the claims has been twice rejected, regardless of whether the claim(s) has/have been finally rejected; the 'twice rejected' limitation does not have to be related to a particular application. Guidance for filing a Notice of Appeal, Appeal Brief and appropriate fees are found in MPEP sections 1204 and 1205.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should follow MPEP procedures for appeals and recognize the procedural rule about 'twice rejected' claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for continued examination (RCE) practice
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.114: If applicant timely files a submission and fee in an application in which prosecution is closed, the office will withdraw the finality of any office action and the submission will be entered and considered; prosecution is closed when under final rejection or appeal, notice of allowance, or actions that otherwise close prosecution (e.g., ex parte Quayle). An RCE is not the filing of a new application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should understand when and how RCEs reopen prosecution and that they are treated as continuing the original application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance, issue, and post-grant procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of Allowability uses form PTOL-37 when an application is placed in condition for allowance; a Notice of Allowance and Issue Fee Due (PTOL-85) normally accompanies a Notice of Allowability. 'Allowance' refers to decision-making; 'Issue' refers to administrative/procedural aspects. An application is ISSUED after a decision to ALLOW; maintenance fees for utility patents due at 3.5, 7.5, and 11.5 years after issue date; corrections by Certificate of Correction or Reissue; fee schedule available on USPTO website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should distinguish allowance from issuance, use appropriate forms, and understand post-issuance maintenance and correction mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview practice and documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO encourages proactive examiner outreach to resolve issues and shorten prosecution; interviews may be telephonic or via WebEx with pro se applicants or attorneys/agents; telephonic/video conference interviews will not be recorded, but the substance will be documented by the examiner in an interview summary; Automated Interview Request (AIR) form is available to schedule interviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should engage in interviews where appropriate, document them properly, and use AIR to schedule. Interviews can aid in resolving issues and may impact prosecution efficiency.
